_README: Fixtures for the publish / discard / error overlays (plan 16 task 1).
THIS FILE IS THE SAME PENDING SESSION THE DASHBOARD SHOWS, AND THE PAGE
PROVES IT RATHER THAN CLAIMING IT. `session.screens` below is the dashboard
fixture's `dirty` state transcribed field for field, and
src/pages/admin/overlays/[...o].astro imports dashboard.json and THROWS if
the entity set or any per-entity change count has drifted. A publish modal
that summarises six changes while the dashboard lists four is the same class
of defect D-15 names for the pipeline strip — two places that must agree —
so here the agreement is a build failure rather than a promise.
WHY `dirty` AND NOT `populated`. Publish and Discard-all are both reached
from a session that has unpublished work on more than one screen, and the
dashboard's `dirty` state is the one that has four. `populated` has three.
THE COUNTS ARE THE FIXTURE'S, NOT UI-SPEC'S EXAMPLE. UI-SPEC's contract
table illustrates the two discard dialogs with `The 6 pending changes on
this screen` and `12 pending changes across 4 screens`. Those are worked
examples, and this session really has 6 changes across 4 screens, of which
Photos owns 2. The copy below therefore says 2 and 6. Plan 15 set this
precedent explicitly for the category-delete dialog (UI-SPEC illustrates it
with `12 photos use it`; Architecture really has 14): a dialog whose entire
job is to state the blast radius may not state it from an example. The
phrase `across 4 screens` survives verbatim because it is true.
NOTHING NON-PUBLIC IS IN HERE. Every string derives from data/*.json,
already committed public site content, by way of src/fixtures/dashboard.json.
No credential, token or Access value appears and none is needed, because
nothing on these routes authenticates, posts or stores (T-00-29).
